title: Choose the billing unit (per seat, flat, usage, per job, per result)
decision_task: Which billing unit fits a business whose product does work for the customer: per person, flat subscription, usage allowance, per completed job/workflow, or per result.
applies_when: Owner is choosing or changing what they charge per (not just how much)
The product or service automates work previously done by staff or contractors
Owner is drawn to outcome or success pricing
exclusions: Pricing is set by a dominant marketplace or regulation
Fewer than a handful of customers and no delivery history (start with a simple fixed offer and learn)
required_inputs: Written outcome definition and attribution method if outcome pricing is considered
evidence_requirements: Can the outcome be defined, measured and attributed to the business without dispute?
Variance of delivery cost per job
Customer's current alternative and its cost (staff time, agency, contractor)
Cash buffer to carry delivery cost before outcome fees are paid
missing_data_behavior: No outcome definition or attribution method: outcome pricing is not eligible; offer base + bonus or per job.
Fewer than a handful of customers: start with a simple fixed offer.
alternatives_when_constrained: Attribution unclear: base fee + capped success bonus
Low volume: fixed-scope package per job
No tracking integration: monthly retainer with a stated volume ceiling

decision_branches.if: Result is measurable, attributable and the owner can carry delivery cost
decision_branches.then: Outcome or success pricing may be tested.
Flat or seat pricing with an add-on for heavy work.

implementation_steps: Describe what the customer values and how they measure it
Gate outcome pricing: measurable + attributable + performance predictable + cash can carry the lag; otherwise drop to workflow or job pricing, or add an outcome bonus on a base fee
Gate per-job/workflow pricing: jobs are standard enough to price; cap or surcharge long-running jobs
Gate usage pricing: volume varies a lot between customers; for small buyers prefer a hybrid (base plan + allowance) over pure pay-as-you-go
Gate replacement framing (price against a hire): the offer covers a defined role's typical output; price as a share of that cost and expect cheaper copycats
Compare two or three candidate models with the owner's own numbers before any price-point optimisation
dependencies: Cash reserve to wait for outcome payments

cash_and_labor_requirements.cash: Outcome pricing delays revenue; the owner must fund delivery until results land

metrics: Contribution per job and per customer
Days from delivery cost to cash received
Win rate and churn by model
guardrails: Outcome definitions written before work starts; no retroactive redefinition
No outcome pricing in regulated categories where contingent fees are restricted without owner/legal review
Show total expected cost range to the buyer
observation_window: One full sales cycle plus one delivery cycle per model tried; outcome models need at least the attribution window plus payment terms.
stop_conditions: Disputes over outcomes exceed an agreed share: move to base + bonus
Workflow jobs run margin-negative repeatedly: add caps or re-scope
Buyers stall on unpredictability: add a base plan or ceiling
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: Plan engine offer/economics stage and Climb AI pricing questions; owner-input form fields (outcome measurability, attribution, cash buffer); new contract field for PB-pricing-test 'billing unit' changes.

interpretation: Interpretation: GU-03's four models map to small-business terms as retainer-per-role, pay-as-you-go, per-job and success fee. The durable content is the gating conditions, not the forecast.
proposed_climbos_rule: Proposed ClimbOS rule: the engine may recommend outcome or success pricing only when the owner confirms a written outcome definition, an attribution method and cash to carry delivery cost; otherwise it offers base + bonus or per-job pricing and explains which gate failed.
disagreements: GU-03 (vendor of outcome billing) says outcome pricing wins long term; GU-02 says no model is perfect and to optimise the current one. For small businesses ClimbOS sides with GU-02 by default; outcome pricing only when the gates pass. GU-04's survey shows small-customer sellers prefer hybrids, consistent with 02_monetization's predictability concern.

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical

inputs_hypothetical.business: Two-person lead-gen agency for local contractors
inputs_hypothetical.attribution: appointments booked through client's own phone line, not tracked

expected_behavior: Flags that attribution is not reliable and cash buffer is thin
Recommends base retainer plus a per-appointment bonus with call tracking, or a fixed package until tracking exists
States the outcome model's preconditions explicitly
hard_failure: Endorsing pure pay-per-result without an attribution method
Citing the guest author's 'outcome pricing will win' as evidence for this business

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
